subject: ClearWave: SLO tradeoffs and cost levers (post-demo action plan)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Monroe <alex@clearwave.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-01-12T15:02:00Z
Subject: Quick post-demo recap + data we need for SLO sizing

Hi Alex — thanks again for the demo time today. Great conversation with your ML infra and platform teams; a few follow-ups so we can size a pilot and confirm cost estimates. I captured the items we agreed on below.

Summary of performance targets you mentioned (please confirm):
- P95 gen latency target: ~150 ms (single-turn, user message -> first token)
- Typical request size: 120 tokens in, 60 tokens out (average)
- Sustained throughput target: 200 req/s during business hours, 800 bursts (10% of traffic)
- Concurrency target: 60 concurrent streams (chat sessions with streaming token output)
- Streaming requirement: server->client token throughput ~200 tokens/sec for sessionized streaming

Immediate data we need from ClearWave to finalize a config and cost ranges:
1) 24-hour sample of request traces or a small representative CSV with: timestamp, input_tokens, output_tokens, is_streaming (Y/N), region.
2) Expected retention window for KV cache (minutes) and any user affinity that would enable prefix caching.
3) Security requirements: KMS/HSM, SOC-2 evidence requests (we can provide our SOC-2 package).

Cost/performance levers we propose to evaluate for your profile:
- Continuous batching tuned to a 25–40 ms batching window for P95 sensitivity; reduces per-token cost for steady traffic.
- Adaptive KV / prefix caching for repeat queries (aim to cut token compute by 15–40% depending on cache locality).
- Mixed quantization profiles: int8 for baseline, int4 for lower-tier variants; fall back to fp16 for high-quality paths.
- Model variant routing: high-quality model for <1% of traffic, mid-size variant for steady-state requests.

Next steps / asks:
- Can you share the trace sample (item #1) by EOD Friday 1/16?
- I'll loop in Lauren and Sergio to propose a two-week pilot config and expected cost ranges once we have the trace.

Attached: redwood-qual-matrix.xlsx (blank template with expected fields).

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Ben — thanks, this is perfect. A couple clarifications from our side before we pull the trace: 

1) The 150 ms P95 is for single-tenant interactive UI flows; backend bulk jobs can be relaxed.
2) For prefix caching: we have ~20% request locality across the top 1,000 users; retention window today is 30 minutes.
3) Streaming behavior: roughly 35% of sessions use streaming with average session length ~5 minutes.

We'll drop a sanitized 24h trace into the sheet you attached (redwood-qual-matrix.xlsx) by close of day Friday. One procurement note: procurement asked for a rough committed-capacity estimate and a sample draft SOW so they can start an internal review.

—Alex

ClearWave Inc.
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-01-13T13:45:00Z
Subject: Internal: suggested pilot config and tradeoffs (notes)

Ben / Sergio — quick draft before I build the pilot config: 

I'll propose two pilot tracks:
A) Latency-optimized (for their 150 ms P95 target)
  - Model: rdm-medium-1 (fp16) primary with rdm-small-1 (int8) fallback for non-critical queries
  - Batching window: 25 ms target (adaptive up to 40 ms on spikes)
  - KV cache: 30 min TTL for session affinity; prefetch top-1000 user prefixes into RAM cache for morning hours
  - Expected compute cost delta: +18% vs baseline but hits P95 consistently

B) Cost-optimized (within 10–15% of latency target)
  - Model: rdm-small-1 (int8) primary with rdm-tiny-1 (int4) for background/low-quality paths
  - Batching window: 40–60 ms (higher savings for steady throughput)
  - Cache aggressive (LRU with 1k-key buffer) — target 25–35% token compute reduction depending on locality
  - Expected compute cost delta: -25% vs baseline, P95 expected ~180–220 ms

Other tradeoffs and operational notes:
- Streaming: enable streaming prioritization lanes so token emission isn't blocked by batching for interactive sessions. That lets us keep perceived latency low while batching in parallel.
- Canary plan: start with 10% traffic on latency-optimized, measure P95 and cost for 72 hours, then move to mixed routing.

I'll assemble expected hourly cost ranges for both tracks once we load the trace. Attaching a simple QoS diagram (clearwave-qos-diagram.png) to illustrate lanes.

—Lauren
Sr. Product Manager, Performance
Redwood Inference
